p.fact: A fact ("timeout is 600 s") is recoverable from the code in a second.
The reason it is 600 s cannot be recovered at all — unless it was written down when the decision was made.

Any choice a future reader could plausibly re-open — a library pick, a constant with consequences, a protocol shape, a rejected approach — gets a **four-field record at the spec anchor that governs the value**:

td.fact: The chosen value or approach. One line.
Concrete and cited: a measurement, a constraint, an incident — with data.
One line per alternative, each carrying its rejection reason.
A measurable trigger: metric + threshold + where it is observed.

p.fact: There is no separate ADR directory and no immutable numbered log.
The spec section that governs the value IS the record; evolution is an edit plus a changelog line; history lives in git.
When the user makes a decision during a session:

item.fact: Propose recording it at the governing anchor, with all four fields, **before the session ends** — an unrecorded decision does not survive the session boundary.
If the why or the trigger is not known, ask. Do not invent data; do not record a two-field stub.
Before changing any value governed by a record, read the record. Re-open it only by naming its trigger state ("the trigger fired: …" / "the trigger has not fired, but …").

p.fact: Trigger design and the periodic sweep: @spec://org.vibevm.world/decision-records/flows/decision-records/revisit-triggers#root.

section.title: Why this matters in a human-AI team

p.fact: The agent cannot ask Vasya why the library was chosen.
It re-derives from what it can read, and the code shows the value, not the constraint — so it re-litigates: "600 s looks arbitrary, propose 300 s for performance."
A recorded decision is immunity from re-litigation.
A recorded trigger is what keeps the immunity from hardening into dogma.

item.fact: Never write "because it is better" — a why cites a measurement, a constraint, or an incident, or it is not a why.
Never re-litigate a recorded decision without naming its trigger state first.
Never put a decision's why into a commit message only. The commit cites the record; the spec carries it.
Never record a decision with a missing reason or a missing revisit trigger — that is a fact with decoration, not a record.
